extracted.name: Tzatziki
extracted.description: Recipe video above. Nobody makes Tzatziki as good as your yiayia, but just in case you want to make one using actual measurements (rather than a little bit of this and a slosh of that!), here is my recipe. Use as a dip for vegetable sticks and warm pita bread, as a sauce for Gyros, Doner kebabs and chicken skewers, and dolloping on Greek baked chicken pieces.
ingredient_lines: 1 1/4 cups Greek yoghurt (or Greek-style yogurt, preferably full fat)
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil ((or more if you want richer))
1/4 heaped teaspoon cooking salt / kosher salt ((halve for table salt, +50% for flakes))
2 tbsp finely chopped dill ((or mint), OPTIONAL - see note)
instruction_lines: Deseed, shred and squeeze - Cut the cucumber in half lengthwise. Use a teaspoon to scrape the watery seeds out. Coarsely grate the cucumber using a box grater. Then wrap in a tea towel and squeeze to remove excess liquid.
Mix - Place cucumber in a bowl. Add remaining ingredients then mix to combine.
Set aside for at least 20 minutes for the flavours to meld.
Use immediately or keep in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days.
